title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout / Go-live Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout planning for the pilot: canary strategy, A/B routing, monitoring and runbooks. Agreed to run two-week canary with 5% traffic ramp, finalize alerting thresholds, and produce an ops runbook and rollback playbook. Redwood to share canary config and metrics dashboard; Vestigo to provide traffic slices and SSO details.
next_steps: Redwood: share canary config + dashboard links by 2026-12-17
Vestigo: send sample traffic slices and SSO metadata by 2026-12-18
Agree on SLOs and alert thresholds by 2026-12-20
action_items: Maya Chen - send canary runbook (v1) and Grafana dashboard links - 2026-12-17
Diego Alvarez - prepare detailed rollback playbook and runbook snippets - 2026-12-18
Liam O'Connor - provide traffic slice definitions and test keys - 2026-12-18

header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Kara Patel (Redwood) — Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez, Noah Patel (Vestigo)
Recording: auto (transcript)
Shared artifacts: canary-runbook-draft.md (Redwood link), pilot-metrics-sheet.xlsx (Vestigo link), security-snapshot.pdf (Redwood link)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off — this is the weekly poc sync focused on the rollout and go-live planning. um quick check, everyone can hear me?
[00:08] Priya Singh: yep, loud and clear. thanks, Maya.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: hi all, Diego here — i'm the se on the account, will cover the canary details and runbook pieces.
[00:18] Priya Singh: great. so our goal today is to lock down the canary, a/b, monitoring and who does what for day zero.
[00:24] Maya Chen: exactly, and align on timelines. quick status: last week we finished the model variant testing, quantization looks good at 4-bit with acceptable latency increase, and we validated prefix caching on your sample traffic.
[00:36] Noah Patel: quick note, on the quantized variant latency sometimes spikes on longer contexts, saw a tail at about 95th percentile, around 1.2s vs 0.9s on non-quant, is that expected?
[00:47] Diego Alvarez: yeah that matches what we observed — the kernel selection sometimes yields higher tail latency for >2k tokens, we can scope a knob to pin a different kernel or force larger batch windows for long contexts, but that increases cost/latency tradeoff.
[00:59] Liam O'Connor: for go-live we want predictable p95 under 1s for our top path, so we need to pick the variant that meets that under realistic traffic.
[01:08] Maya Chen: understood. proposal: canary stage 1 uses hosted Redwood model-variant A (non-quant) for 5% traffic for 3 days, stage 2 moves 25% for 4 days on quant variant B with pinned kernel, monitor p50/p95, error rate, and cost delta. canary rollbacks automatic if error rate >0.5% or p95 >1.2s for 1 hour.
[01:28] Priya Singh: 3 days feels long, can we do 48 hours? we need to balance speed vs safety.
[01:33] Diego Alvarez: we can shorten to 48 hours for stage 1, but recommend 72 for stage 2 because load pattern variance shows up after 1-2 days. stage 2 is when A/B hits more production-like slices.
[01:45] Sofia Martinez: security question — during canary will logs with user PII ever leave the VPC? we need confirmation on KMS and log retention.
[01:53] Maya Chen: all logs are stored in customer-configured s3 with KMS keys if you're on private; for hosted we can set a dedicated key and mask PII at ingestion. we'll attach the security-snapshot and the kms integration doc after the call.
[02:05] Sofia Martinez: and audit logs — we need admin audit trails for calls, ideally sent to our SIEM.
[02:10] Diego Alvarez: yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or a push integration; we'll include an example config.
[02:16] Priya Singh: good. on A/B testing — we want to experiment with a threshold-based routing to route edge cases to fallback model, is that possible?
[02:24] Diego Alvarez: yep, policy routing supports predicate rules — e.g., if request length > 1500 tokens or presence of certain metadata route to fallback dedicated model or higher-cost variant. we can codify rules in route config.
[02:34] Liam O'Connor: for canary instrumentation we need dashboards for p50/p95, tokens/sec, model queue depth, kv cache hit rate, and cost per 1k tokens. can you share dashboard templates?
[02:45] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll share Grafana dashboard links; Diego will add panels for kv cache hit/miss and batching metrics.
[02:51] Diego Alvarez: i'll also add traces showing internal queue times — that helps identify where tail latency originates.
[02:57] Priya Singh: great. what about rollback mechanics, specifically who executes automatic vs manual rollback?
[03:03] Maya Chen: automatic rollback is triggered by the policy (error rate or p95 breach) and will fallback to previous variant or route to dedicated capacity; manual rollback is run by your on-call platform engineer with the rollback runbook steps we provide.
[03:15] Noah Patel: can we do a dry-run where the rollback is simulated but not executed, to validate alerting and playbook?
[03:21] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can run a dry-run mode where alerts are fired and an incident is created in your pager, without flipping traffic — great idea for the 12/22 dry-run.
[03:31] Priya Singh: timeline stuff: if we want live in early Jan, what's the gating?
[03:36] Maya Chen: gating items are: SSO/SAML integration complete, runbooks and rollback validated, monitoring and alert thresholds agreed, and a final 48-72h canary with real traffic. also SOC2/contract signoff but that's parallel.
[03:48] Sofia Martinez: contract side — our legal needs the data retention and encryption clauses, and Redwood's SOC2 scope. Kara, can you follow up?
[03:55] Kara Patel: yes, I'll send the SOC2 snapshot and our standard data processing addendum, and link to last quarter's security attestation.
[04:03] Priya Singh: ok next piece — sampling: we'll provide traffic slices by user cohort; we want to avoid skew. Noah will define cohorts.
[04:10] Noah Patel: i'll produce slices — top 10% power users, random 1% baseline, and two edge-case cohorts. will share by Friday.
[04:18] Maya Chen: perfect. Diego, on monitoring thresholds, what default thresholds do you recommend for the canary?
[04:24] Diego Alvarez: default: error rate >0.5% over 15m sliding, p95 breach >1.2s for 30m, token-queue depth >50 for 10m, kv cache hit rate drop >10% from baseline. those are conservative but safe.
[04:38] Liam O'Connor: can we tune p95 to 1.0s once we're confident?
[04:41] Diego Alvarez: yes, SLOs can be tightened after canary passes. we should codify SLO targets in the runbook.
[04:47] Priya Singh: testing — we need load tests that emulate peak morning traffic and batch patterns. who owns load testing?
[04:53] Maya Chen: joint — Redwood can provide a load harness script and sample profile, Vestigo to run against staging and share results; Diego will prepare the harness.
[05:01] Diego Alvarez: i'll post the harness and a runbook. include steps to generate KV warmup traffic so prefix cache behaves like prod.
[05:09] Sofia Martinez: compliance question on data residency — logs must stay in eu-west-1 for EU users. can routing be region-aware?
[05:16] Maya Chen: yes, region-aware routing supported; for hosted we can set a region policy to process EU requests in eu-west-1 and also pin storage accordingly.
[05:25] Priya Singh: ok, walk me through a typical cutover plan at high-level?
[05:29] Diego Alvarez: high-level: 1) Prep: config, dashboards, SSO, keys; 2) Dry-run: alerts simulated, no traffic flip (12/22); 3) Canary stage 1: 5% traffic 48h non-quant variant; 4) Evaluate metrics + security checks; 5) Canary stage 2: 25% quant variant 72h; 6) Ramp to 50% then to 100% with monitoring gates; 7) Post-cutover review and rollback window. we'll provide a cutover checklist.
[05:54] Priya Singh: sounds good. on A/B experiments during canary, will traffic be split randomly or by cohort?
[05:59] Diego Alvarez: routing supports random and deterministic cohort hashing — deterministic is better if you want sticky sessions for users.
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: sticky hashing is preferred.
[06:07] Maya Chen: noted. any concerns on cost exposure during canary?
[06:11] Noah Patel: yes, quant variant increases cost by around 10% in our estimate due to pinning kernels, need cost cap alert.
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: we can set cost-per-1k token alerts and implement throttles if cost exceeds X. we'll include those panels.
[06:25] Priya Singh: good. Kara, legal/SOC follow ups?
[06:28] Kara Patel: will share DPA and SOC2 links; also include a runbook for data deletion requests.
[06:33] Priya Singh: ok, anything else?
[06:35] Diego Alvarez: one more technical note — if you plan to move to Redwood Dedicated later, the rollout plan stays the same but we'll map dedicated pools as fallback target; keep that in mind.
[06:46] Priya Singh: yes, likely move to dedicated after pilot. timeline depends on pilot metrics.
[06:50] Maya Chen: recap of next steps — we'll send canary runbook v1 and Grafana dash by 12/17; Diego sends rollback playbook by 12/18; Vestigo sends traffic slices and SAML metadata by 12/18; dry-run scheduled 12/22; agree on final SLOs by 12/20.
[07:06] Priya Singh: that's clear. thanks team.
[07:09] Maya Chen: cool, we'll follow up in email with links. thanks everyone.
[07:12] [meeting ends]
